findings.description: The bucket has no ACL set explicitly and is commented as public, meaning it likely uses the default public-read/write configuration or a public ACL, exposing potentially sensitive data (it stores a customer master file) to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including customer data) are not encrypted at rest.
The bucket does not enable versioning, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss/overwrite without ability to recover prior versions.
The bucket does not have access logging enabled, making it difficult to detect or investigate unauthorized access to sensitive data.
A customer master spreadsheet (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is publicly accessible and unencrypted, exposing potentially sensitive customer information.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving sensitive data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled on the financials bucket, risking permanent data loss from accidental deletion or overwrite of financial records.
No access logging is configured for the financials bucket, hindering detection of unauthorized access to sensitive financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operations data stored unencrypted at rest.
No access logging is configured for the operations bucket, hindering detection of unauthorized or anomalous access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the data_science bucket, leaving its contents unencrypted at rest.
